title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Third Batch of Guiding Cases
ruling_gist_en: Shareholders of a limited liability company, and directors and controlling shareholders of a company limited by shares, shall perform the obligation of liquidation after the company's business license is revoked in accordance with the law. They may not be exempted from the liquidation obligation on the grounds that they are not actual controllers or did not actually participate in the company's operation and management.
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the Third Batch of Guiding Cases

Fa [2012] No. 227

Higher People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the Higher People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

Upon deliberation and decision by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court, the following four cases (Guiding Cases No. 9-12), including the dispute over a sales contract between Shanghai Cunliang Trading Co., Ltd. and Jiang Zhidong, Wang Weiming, et al., are hereby published as the third batch of guiding cases for reference in adjudicating similar cases.

September 18, 2012

Guiding Case No. 9

Shanghai Cunliang Trading Co., Ltd. v. Jiang Zhidong, Wang Weiming, et al. — dispute over a sales contract

(Adopted by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court, issued on September 18, 2012)

Keywords: Civil; Obligation of liquidation of a company; Joint and several liability for repayment

Ruling Gist

Shareholders of a limited liability company, and directors and controlling shareholders of a joint stock limited company, shall perform their liquidation obligations in accordance with the law after the company's business license is revoked. They may not be exempted from such liquidation obligations on the grounds that they are not actual controllers or that they did not actually participate in the company's operation and management.

Relevant Legal Provisions

Articles 20 and 184 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China

Basic Facts

The plaintiff, Shanghai Cunliang Trading Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Cunliang Company), alleged that it supplied steel products to the defendant, Changzhou Tuoheng Mechanical Equipment Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Tuoheng Company), and Tuoheng Company still owed RMB 1,395,228.6 in payment for goods. The defendants Fang Hengfu, Jiang Zhidong, and Wang Weiming were shareholders of Tuoheng Company. Tuoheng Company failed to undergo annual inspection, and its business license was revoked by the administrative department for industry and commerce. To date, no liquidation has been organized. Due to their failure to perform liquidation obligations, the company's property was dissipated or lost, and Cunliang Company's claims could not be satisfied. According to the Company Law and relevant judicial interpretations, Fang Hengfu, Jiang Zhidong, and Wang Weiming should bear joint and several liability for Tuoheng Company's debts. Therefore, the plaintiff requested the court to order Tuoheng Company to repay RMB 1,395,228.6 in payment for goods plus liquidated damages, and to order Fang Hengfu, Jiang Zhidong, and Wang Weiming to bear joint and several liability for repayment of Tuoheng Company's debts.

The defendants Jiang Zhidong and Wang Weiming argued in their defense: (1) Neither of them had ever participated in the operation or management of Tuoheng Company; (2) Tuoheng Company was actually controlled by the major shareholder Fang Hengfu, and they were unable to liquidate the company; (3) Due to poor management, Tuoheng Company had already incurred substantial debts and was insolvent before its business license was revoked, and the dissipation of Tuoheng Company's property was not caused by Jiang Zhidong or Wang Weiming's failure to perform liquidation obligations; (4) Jiang Zhidong and Wang Weiming had also entrusted a lawyer to liquidate Tuoheng Company, but the liquidation could not be carried out because Tuoheng Company's property was repeatedly looted by creditors. Therefore, Jiang Zhidong and Wang Weiming did not fail to perform their liquidation obligations. Accordingly, they requested the court to dismiss Cunliang Company's claims against Jiang Zhidong and Wang Weiming.

The defendants Tuoheng Company and Fang Hengfu did not appear in court and did not submit any defense.

Facts Found by the Court: On June 28, 2007, Cunliang Company and Tuoheng Company entered into a steel products sales contract. Cunliang Company fulfilled its supply obligation in the amount of RMB 7,095,006.6. Tuoheng Company had paid RMB 5,699,778, leaving an outstanding balance of RMB 1,395,228.6. In addition, Fang Hengfu, Jiang Zhidong, and Wang Weiming were shareholders of Tuoheng Company, with shareholdings of 40%, 30%, and 30%, respectively. Tuoheng Company failed to undergo annual inspection, and its business license was revoked by the administrative department for industry and commerce on December 25, 2008. To date, the shareholders have not organized a liquidation. Currently, Tuoheng Company has no office or place of business, and its account books and property are all missing. In other cases, enforcement proceedings against Tuoheng Company were suspended due to a lack of available property.

Judgment

The Songjiang District People's Court of Shanghai rendered a civil judgment on December 8, 2009 ((2009) Song Min Er (Shang) Chu Zi No. 1052): 1. Tuoheng Company shall pay Cunliang Company RMB 1,395,228.6 in payment for goods plus corresponding liquidated damages; 2. Fang Hengfu, Jiang Zhidong, and Wang Weiming shall bear joint and several liability for repayment of the above debts of Tuoheng Company. After the judgment was pronounced, Jiang Zhidong and Wang Weiming appealed. The Shanghai No. 1 Intermediate People's Court rendered a civil judgment on September 1, 2010 ((2010) Hu Yi Zhong Min Si (Shang) Zhong Zi No. 1302), dismissing the appeal and affirming the original judgment.

Reasoning

The effective judgment of the court held that: After Cunliang Company delivered the goods in accordance with the contract, Tuoheng Company failed to pay the full amount as agreed, and therefore should bear the corresponding payment liability and liability for breach of contract. As shareholders of Tuoheng Company, Fang Hengfu, Jiang Zhidong, and Wang Weiming should have promptly organized a liquidation after Tuoheng Company's business license was revoked. Because Fang Hengfu, Jiang Zhidong, and Wang Weiming failed to perform their liquidation obligations, the main assets and account books of Tuoheng Company were lost, making it impossible to liquidate. The failure of Fang Hengfu, Jiang Zhidong, and Wang Weiming to perform their liquidation obligations violated the relevant provisions of the Company Law and its judicial interpretations, and therefore they should bear joint and several liability for repayment of Tuoheng Company's debts. As a limited liability company, all shareholders of Tuoheng Company should, in law, collectively become the persons obligated to liquidate the company. The Company Law and its relevant judicial interpretations do not provide for the exception clauses argued by Jiang Zhidong and Wang Weiming. Therefore, regardless of the proportion of shares held by Jiang Zhidong and Wang Weiming in Tuoheng Company, and whether they actually participated in the company's operation and management, both were obligated to lawfully liquidate Tuoheng Company within the statutory period after its business license was revoked. Regarding the argument by Jiang Zhidong and Wang Weiming that Tuoheng Company had already incurred substantial debts before its business license was revoked, and that even if they had failed to perform their liquidation obligations, there was no causal link with the loss of Tuoheng Company's property, according to the facts found, the suspension of enforcement proceedings in other cases due to a lack of available property of Tuoheng Company only shows that the court did not find any property of Tuoheng Company during enforcement, but does not prove that all of Tuoheng Company's property was lost before its business license was revoked. There is a causal link between the failure of Tuoheng Company's three shareholders to perform their liquidation obligations and the loss of Tuoheng Company's property and account books. Therefore, the defense raised by Jiang Zhidong and Wang Weiming on this point is not established. The entrustment contract for liquidation signed by Jiang Zhidong and Wang Weiming with a lawyer and the lawyer's certificate only show that Jiang Zhidong and Wang Weiming intended to liquidate Tuoheng Company, but in fact the liquidation of Tuoheng Company was not carried out. Accordingly, it cannot be determined that Jiang Zhidong and Wang Weiming lawfully performed their liquidation obligations, and therefore this defense of Jiang Zhidong and Wang Weiming is not accepted.

Guiding Case No. 10

Li Jianjun v. Shanghai Jia Dongli Environmental Protection Technology Co., Ltd. — dispute over revocation of a company resolution

(Adopted by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court, issued on September 18, 2012)

Keywords: Civil; Revocation of company resolution; Scope of judicial review

Ruling Gist

When hearing a dispute over the revocation of a company resolution, a people's court shall examine whether the procedures for convening the meeting and the methods of voting violate laws, administrative regulations, or the company's articles of association, and whether the content of the resolution violates the company's articles of association. Provided that the above provisions are not violated, whether the facts on which the resolution to dismiss the general manager are true and whether the reasons are valid do not fall within the scope of judicial review.

Relevant Legal Provisions

Paragraph 2 of Article 22 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China

Basic Facts

The plaintiff, Li Jianjun, alleged that the facts and reasons on which the defendant, Shanghai Jia Dongli Environmental Protection Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jia Dongli Company), based its resolution to remove him from the position of general manager were not established, and that the procedures for convening the board meeting, the methods of voting, and the content of the resolution all violated the provisions of the Company Law. He requested the court to revoke the board resolution in accordance with the law.

The defendant, Jia Dongli Company, argued in its defense that the procedures for convening the board meeting, the methods of voting, and the content of the resolution all complied with the provisions of the law and the company's articles of association, and therefore the board resolution was valid.

Facts Found by the Court: The plaintiff, Li Jianjun, was a shareholder of the defendant Jia Dongli Company and served as its general manager. The shareholding structure of Jia Dongli Company was as follows: Ge Yongle held 40%, Li Jianjun held 46%, and Wang Taisheng held 14%. The three shareholders jointly formed the board of directors, with Ge Yongle serving as chairman and the other two as directors. The company's articles of association provided that the board of directors exercised powers including the appointment or dismissal of the company's manager; a board meeting was valid only if attended by more than two-thirds of the directors; and resolutions on matters discussed at the meeting were valid only if passed by more than two-thirds of the directors representing all shareholders. On July 18, 2009, Ge Yongle, the chairman of Jia Dongli Company, convened and presided over a board meeting, attended by all three directors. The meeting adopted a resolution stating: "In view of the fact that General Manager Li Jianjun, without the consent of the board of directors, used company funds to engage in stock trading in the secondary market, causing huge losses, his position as General Manager is hereby removed, effective immediately." The resolution was signed by Ge Yongle, Wang Taisheng, and the supervisor, but Li Jianjun did not sign it.

Judgment

The Huangpu District People's Court of Shanghai rendered a civil judgment on February 5, 2010 ((2009) Huang Min Er (Shang) Chu Zi No. 4569), revoking the board resolution formed by the defendant Jia Dongli Company on July 18, 2009. After the judgment was pronounced, Jia Dongli Company appealed. The Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court rendered a civil judgment on June 4, 2010 ((2010) Hu Er Zhong Min Si (Shang) Zhong Zi No. 436): 1. Setting aside the civil judgment of the Huangpu District People's Court of Shanghai ((2009) Huang Min Er (Shang) Chu Zi No. 4569); 2. Dismissing Li Jianjun's claims.

Reasoning

The effective judgment of the court held that: According to the provisions of Paragraph 2 of Article 22 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China, the grounds for revocation of a board resolution include: (1) the convening procedures violate laws, administrative regulations, or the company's articles of association; (2) the voting methods violate laws, administrative regulations, or the company's articles of association; (3) the content of the resolution violates the company's articles of association. As to the convening procedures, the board meeting of Jia Dongli Company held on July 18, 2009 was convened by Chairman Ge Yongle, and all three directors attended the meeting. The convening procedures of this board meeting did not violate the provisions of laws, administrative regulations, or the company's articles of association. As to the voting methods, according to Jia Dongli Company's articles of association, resolutions on matters discussed at the meeting were valid only if passed by more than two-thirds of the directors representing all shareholders. The above board resolution was passed by two of the three shareholders (who were also directors). Therefore, the voting methods did not violate laws, administrative regulations, or the company's articles of association. As to the content of the resolution, Jia Dongli Company's articles of association provided that the board of directors had the power to dismiss the company's manager. The statement in the board resolution that "General Manager Li Jianjun, without the consent of the board of directors, used company funds to engage in stock trading in the secondary market, causing huge losses" was merely the reason for the board's decision to dismiss Li Jianjun from his position as General Manager. The content of the resolution to dismiss Li Jianjun from the position of General Manager itself did not violate the company's articles of association.

If the reason for the board's resolution to dismiss Li Jianjun from the position of General Manager did not exist, that alone would not lead to the revocation of the board resolution. First, the Company Law respects company autonomy; internal legal relationships within a company are, in principle, governed by the company's autonomous mechanisms, and judicial authorities do not, in principle, intervene in internal company affairs. Second, Jia Dongli Company's articles of association did not impose any restrictions on the board's power to dismiss the company's manager; it did not provide that the board must have a specific reason to dismiss the company's manager. The content of the articles of association did not violate mandatory provisions of the Company Law and should be deemed valid. Therefore, the board of Jia Dongli Company could exercise the powers conferred by the company's articles of association and make a decision to dismiss the company's manager. Accordingly, the court should respect company autonomy and need not examine whether the reason for the board of Jia Dongli Company to dismiss the company's manager existed, i.e., it need not examine whether the facts on which the resolution was based were true or whether the reasons were valid. In summary, Li Jianjun's claim for revocation of the board resolution was not established and was lawfully dismissed.

Guiding Case No. 11

Yang Yanhu et al. — embezzlement case

(Adopted by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court, issued on September 18, 2012)

Keywords: Criminal; Crime of embezzlement; Convenience of official position; Defrauding of land use rights

Ruling Gist

1. "Taking advantage of one's official position" in the crime of embezzlement refers to taking advantage of the power and convenient conditions for supervising, managing, or handling public property in one's official position. It includes not only taking advantage of one's own official position to supervise or manage public property, but also taking advantage of the official positions of other state functionaries who are subordinate to one's own official position.

2. Land use rights constitute property interests and fall within the category of "public property" as provided in Paragraph 1 of Article 382 of the Criminal Law, and thus may be the object of embezzlement.

Relevant Legal Provisions

Paragraph 1 of Article 382 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China

Basic Facts

The defendant Yang Yanhu served as a member of the Standing Committee of the Yiwu Municipal Committee of the Communist Party of China from August 1996; as the Deputy Director of the Standing Committee of the Yiwu Municipal People's Congress from March 2003; and concurrently as the Deputy Head of the Construction Leading Group and the Commander-in-Chief of the Headquarters for the Construction of the China Small Commodity City Futian Market (renamed the China Yiwu International Trade Mart, hereinafter referred to as the International Trade Mart) from August 2000, responsible for the overall work of the headquarters. In 2002, Yang Yanhu learned that Gonghe Village, Choucheng Subdistrict, Yiwu City, would be included in the scope of demolition and old village renovation, and decided to purchase an old house in that village, using his official position to defraud illegal benefits during the demolition and resettlement process. Yang Yanhu then conspired with the defendants Wang Yuefang (Yang Yanhu's wife's younger sister) and Zheng Xinchao (Wang Yuefang's husband). Wang and Zheng, acting on their own behalf, through a person named Wang of Gonghe Village, purchased three old houses of a person named Zhao in the village in the name of Wang Yuefang (registered area of the property certificate: 61.87 square meters; date of certificate issuance: August 3, 1998). According to local demolition and old village renovation policies, regardless of whether Zhao owned those old houses, the area of resettlement land to which he was entitled was the same; in fact, Zhao was resettled with land as a person without a house. In March or April 2003, in order to have the land occupied by the three old houses confirmed under Wang Yuefang's name, under the direction and arrangement of Yang Yanhu, Zheng Xinchao again contacted the person named Wang of Gonghe Village to have the village committee and its members issue a false certificate stating that the three old houses were built by Wang Yuefang in 1983. Yang Yanhu took advantage of his official position and requested Wu Moumou, the Deputy Commander-in-Chief of the International Trade Mart Construction Headquarters, who was concurrently in charge of land confirmation work and also the Deputy Director of the Yiwu Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources, as well as the staff of the headquarters' land confirmation and approval section, to give favorable treatment to Wang Yuefang's demolition resettlement and land confirmation. The International Trade Mart Construction Headquarters then processed the purchased house as an old house with a village certificate but without a property certificate for land confirmation review, and submitted it to the Yiwu Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources for confirmation, and based on the measurement results, determined the land area as 64.7 square meters.

Subsequently, the defendants Yang Yanhu, Zheng Xinchao, and Wang Yuefang conspired again. Based on the fact that Yang Yanhu's father-in-law Wang Mouxiang was entitled to a land confirmation of 25.5 square meters in the demolition of Gonghe Village, they fabricated an application report signed by Wang Yuefang and others in January 2005, falsely stating that "Wang Mouxiang and Wang Yuefang jointly owned three and a half houses covering an area of 90.2 square meters; they divided the property in 1986, with Wang Mouxiang receiving 36.1 square meters and Wang Yuefang receiving 54.1 square meters; the relevant authorities mistakenly confirmed Wang Mouxiang's house as 25.5 square meters and Wang Yuefang's house as 64 square meters," requesting a correction from the Yiwu Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources. Then, Yang Yanhu took advantage of his official position and directed the staff of the International Trade Mart Construction Headquarters to stamp the application report with the seal of the headquarters for confirmation, and caused the application report to be approved by the Yiwu Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources and the Yiwu Municipal Government, thereby allowing Wang Yuefang and Wang Mouxiang to respectively obtain construction land approvals of 72 square meters and 54 square meters (totaling 126 square meters). Based on Wang Mouxiang's confirmed land area, he should have only received 36 square meters of construction land approval; the remaining 90 square meters were illegally obtained. In May 2005, after paying a site selection fee of RMB 245,520, Yang Yanhu and others obtained demolition resettlement compensation for two shop units with a land area of 72 square meters in the demolition resettlement area of the International Trade Mart (after the case was uncovered, the land use rights for these 72 square meters were frozen according to law). The plot had been expropriated by the state and converted to construction land before being used for resettlement; it was state-owned allocated land. According to an appraisal, the land use rights at this location were valued at RMB 35,270 per square meter. The 90 square meters of construction land illegally obtained by Yang Yanhu and others, when converted according to local demolition resettlement regulations, corresponded to a shop land area of 72 square meters in the demolition resettlement area, with a value of RMB 2,539,440. After deducting the RMB 245,520 they paid, the actual illegal gains amounted to RMB 2,293,920.

In addition, between 2001 and 2007, the defendant Yang Yanhu took advantage of his official position to seek benefits for others in contracting projects, demolition resettlement, and acquisition of state-owned land, and illegally accepted or extorted a total of RMB 570,000, including RMB 50,000 in extortion.

Judgment

The Jinhua Intermediate People's Court of Zhejiang Province rendered a criminal judgment on December 15, 2008 ((2008) Jin Zhong Xing Er Chu Zi No. 30): 1. The defendant Yang Yanhu was convicted of the crime of embezzlement and sentenced to 15 years' imprisonment, with a concurrent fine of RMB 200,000 in confiscation of property; convicted of the crime of accepting bribes and sentenced to 11 years' imprisonment, with a concurrent fine of RMB 100,000 in confiscation of property; the combined sentence was 18 years' imprisonment, with a concurrent fine of RMB 300,000 in confiscation of property. 2. The defendant Zheng Xinchao was convicted of the crime of embezzlement and sentenced to 5 years' imprisonment. 3. The defendant Wang Yuefang was convicted of the crime of embezzlement and sentenced to 3 years' imprisonment. After the judgment was pronounced, all three defendants appealed. The Zhejiang High People's Court rendered a criminal ruling on March 16, 2009 ((2009) Zhe Xing Er Zhong Zi No. 34), dismissing the appeal and affirming the original judgment.

Reasoning

The effective judgment of the court held that: Regarding the defense argument raised by Yang Yanhu's defense counsel that Yang Yanhu did not take advantage of his official position, the court found that the International Trade Mart Construction Headquarters was an institution established by the Yiwu Municipal Party Committee and the Yiwu Municipal Government to ensure the smooth progress of the International Trade Mart construction project. The headquarters had a Land Confirmation and Approval Section, whose staff were seconded from the Bureau of Land and Resources and were responsible for land confirmation, review, and approval of construction land. The Deputy Commander-in-Chief in charge of this section, Wu Moumou, was also a deputy director of the Bureau of Land and Resources. The Land Confirmation and Approval Section, as a subordinate unit of the headquarters, was subject to the leadership of the headquarters. Yang Yanhu, as the Commander-in-Chief of the headquarters, had the authority to lead this section. "Taking advantage of one's official position" in the crime of embezzlement refers to taking advantage of the power and convenient conditions for supervising, managing, or handling public property in one's official position. It includes not only taking advantage of one's own official position to supervise or manage public property, but also taking advantage of the official positions of other state functionaries who are subordinate to one's own official position. In this case, Yang Yanhu took advantage of his official positions as a member of the Standing Committee of the Yiwu Municipal Committee of the Communist Party of China, Deputy Director of the Standing Committee of the Yiwu Municipal People's Congress, and concurrent Commander-in-Chief of the Headquarters to give instructions to the staff of the land confirmation and approval section and the Deputy Commander-in-Chief in charge, thereby enabling Wang Yuefang and others to achieve the false demolition resettlement.

Regarding the defense opinion raised by the defendant Yang Yanhu and others as well as their defense counsel that defendant Wang Yuefang should receive land resettlement compensation and that the land involved is collective land, which cannot constitute the crime of embezzlement. Upon investigation, when Wang Yuefang purchased the house, she had a non-agricultural household registration. According to the law and the relevant provisions on demolition and resettlement in Yiwu City, she was not a qualified subject for demolition and resettlement and did not have the eligibility to obtain land confirmation. The house she purchased in Gonghe Village could neither obtain land confirmation nor receive demolition resettlement compensation. Yang Yanhu and others, knowing that Wang Yuefang did not meet the conditions for demolition resettlement, took advantage of Yang Yanhu's official position to fabricate the purchased house as her ancestral old house and fabricated the facts of Wang Yuefang's separation from Wang Mouxiang, thereby fraudulently obtaining the qualification for old house demolition resettlement and illegally obtaining confirmation of state-owned land rights. At the same time, because Yang Yanhu used his official position, Yang Yanhu, Wang Yuefang, and others engaged in fraud, causing Zhao Moumou, the owner of the old house purchased by Wang Yuefang, to receive land resettlement compensation as a person without a house, and also enabling Wang Yuefang, who should not have received land resettlement compensation, to obtain it. Articles 2 and 9 of the Land Administration Law of the People's Republic of China stipulate that land in China shall be under socialist public ownership, namely ownership by the whole people and collective ownership by the working masses, and may be lawfully allocated to units or individuals for use. The possession, use, development, operation, transaction, and circulation of land can bring corresponding economic benefits. Therefore, the right to use land naturally has property interests. Whether it is state-owned land or collective land, it falls within the scope of "public property" as stipulated in Article 382, Paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law and can be the object of embezzlement. The land allocated under Wang Yuefang's name had already been requisitioned as state-owned and converted to construction land in August 2002, and the Yiwu City Government document copy also clearly states that the demolition resettlement land use right registration for this area shall issue a state-owned land use right certificate. Therefore, the defense opinion raised by Yang Yanhu and others and their defense counsel cannot stand. In summary, defendant Yang Yanhu, as a state functionary, took advantage of his positions as a member of the Yiwu Municipal Committee of the CPC, Deputy Director of the Yiwu Municipal People's Congress Standing Committee, and concurrently as General Commander of the International Trade City Headquarters, and in collusion with defendants Zheng Xinchao and Wang Yuefang, using means of fabricating facts, fraudulently obtained the right to use state-owned land and illegally possessed public property. The actions of the three defendants all constituted the crime of embezzlement. Yang Yanhu also took advantage of his official position to extort or accept bribes from others and sought benefits for others, and his actions also constituted the crime of bribery, for which he should be punished for multiple crimes in accordance with the law. In the joint embezzlement crime, Yang Yanhu played a principal role and was the principal offender, and shall be punished for all the crimes he participated in or organized and commanded. Zheng Xinchao and Wang Yuefang played secondary roles and were accomplices, and their punishments should be mitigated. Therefore, the courts of first and second instance rendered the above judgment in accordance with the law.

Guiding Case No. 12

Li Fei — intentional homicide case

(Discussed and approved by the Adjudication Committee of the Supreme People's Court, released on September 18, 2012)

Keywords: Criminal, intentional homicide, dispute arising from non-antagonistic conflicts in daily life, family members assisting in arrest, recidivism, death sentence with a two-year reprieve, restriction on commutation of sentence

Ruling Gist

For an intentional homicide case arising from non-antagonistic conflicts in daily life, where the defendant's criminal methods are cruel and the defendant is a recidivist, and the crime warrants the death penalty, but the defendant's family members voluntarily and actively assist the public security authorities in arresting the defendant and actively make compensation, the people's court may, in light of the specific circumstances of the case and from the perspective of resolving social conflicts to the greatest extent, impose a death sentence with a two-year reprieve and also impose a restriction on commutation of sentence.

Related Legal Provision

Paragraph 2 of Article 50 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China

Basic Facts

On April 14, 2006, defendant Li Fei was sentenced to two years of fixed-term imprisonment for theft and was released upon completion of the sentence on January 2, 2008. In April 2008, Li Fei established a romantic relationship with the victim Xu Moumou (female, 26 years old at the time of death) through an introduction. In August of the same year, they broke up due to frequent arguments. On August 24, when the local public security authorities went to Li Fei's workplace to establish a key person file for him, his employer learned that Li Fei had been sentenced for a crime and terminated his employment on that basis. Li Fei believed that his termination was related to Xu Moumou.

At approximately 9:00 p.m. on September 12, 2008, defendant Li Fei called Xu Moumou's mobile phone. Since Xu Moumou was out, her cousin Wang Moumou (victim, then 16 years old) answered the call and told Li Fei that Xu Moumou had gone out. Subsequently, Li Fei called Xu Moumou's mobile phone multiple times but received no answer. At around 11:00 p.m. that day, Li Fei went near the "Little Angel Image Design Studio" run by Xu Moumou in Hulan District, Harbin City, and called Xu Moumou's phone again, engaging in a quarrel over the phone. Li Fei then broke into Xu Moumou's bedroom inside the "Little Angel Image Design Studio" and struck Xu Moumou's head multiple times with a hammer from the room, and also struck the head and hands of Xu Moumou's cousin Wang Moumou several times. Shortly thereafter, Li Fei struck the heads of Xu Moumou and Wang Moumou again with the hammer, causing Xu Moumou's death at the scene and minor injuries to Wang Moumou. To prevent the apprentice Tong Mou from calling the police, Li Fei took the mobile phones of Xu Moumou, Wang Moumou, and Tong Mou away from the scene and discarded them, then fled. At around 10:00 p.m. on September 23, Li Fei went to the home of his aunt Li Moumou and asked her to convey to his mother Liang Moumou to send money. Upon learning the situation, Liang Moumou promptly reported to the public security authorities and assisted them in capturing Li Fei when he came to his aunt's home to collect the money the following evening. During the trial, Li Fei's mother Liang Moumou compensated the victim's family members with RMB 40,000.

Judgment

The Harbin Intermediate People's Court of Heilongjiang Province rendered a criminal judgment (2009) Ha Xing Er Chu Zi No. 51 on April 30, 2009, finding defendant Li Fei guilty of intentional homicide and sentencing him to death, deprivation of political rights for life. After the judgment was pronounced, Li Fei appealed. The Heilongjiang High People's Court issued a criminal ruling (2009) Hei Xing San Zhong Zi No. 70 on October 29, 2009, dismissing the appeal and affirming the original judgment, and submitted it to the Supreme People's Court for approval in accordance with the law. Based on the confirmed facts upon review and the fact that the defendant's mother assisted in his arrest, the Supreme People's Court issued a criminal ruling (2010) Xing Wu Fu 66820039, disapproving the death sentence for defendant Li Fei and remanding the case to the Heilongjiang High People's Court for retrial. After a new trial in accordance with the law, the Heilongjiang High People's Court rendered a criminal judgment (2011) Hei Xing San Zhong Zi No. 63 on May 3, 2011, sentencing defendant Li Fei to death, with a two-year reprieve, and deprivation of political rights for life, and simultaneously imposing a restriction on commutation of sentence.

Reasoning

Upon retrial, the Heilongjiang High People's Court found that: The actions of defendant Li Fei constituted the crime of intentional homicide. His crime was extremely serious and warranted the death penalty as a matter of law. This case was a crime arising from non-antagonistic conflicts in daily life. After the crime, when Li Fei's mother Liang Moumou learned of Li Fei's whereabouts after the homicide, she voluntarily and promptly reported to the public security authorities and actively cooperated with them to capture Li Fei. When the public security authorities arrested Li Fei, he complied without resistance and truthfully confessed all his criminal facts after arrest, demonstrating a good attitude toward confession. During the trial, Li Fei's mother compensated the victim's economic losses on his behalf. Although Li Fei was a recidivist, his previous theft was relatively minor. Considering these circumstances comprehensively, leniency could be granted to Li Fei, and he need not be sentenced to death with immediate execution. At the same time, given the cruelty of his intentional homicide methods, his status as a recidivist, and the lack of forgiveness from the victim's family, Li Fei was lawfully sentenced to death with a two-year reprieve, with the imposition of a restriction on commutation of sentence.
